derivation_notes: The parent already assumes that exposed ends amplify monomer self-limitation, but it uses a linear-in-E amplifier. Here that coefficient is made E-dependent in a sharper saturating way, replacing E/E_self_amp by E/(E_self_amp + E), which preserves the dilute-end linear limit while producing stronger high-E curvature in G sweeps.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption that end-driven amplification of monomer self-limitation grows proportionally without saturation. The refined law keeps low-E behavior close to the parent but makes monomer-side bending emerge more abruptly once end abundance becomes comparable to or larger than E_self_amp.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: End-rich demand amplifies monomer self-limitation in a proportionally linear way with E through G_self/(1 + E/E_self_amp).
assumption_audit.mechanism: Local competition among many nearby filament ends for a partially shared immediately addable monomer subpool can intensify nonlinearly and then saturate, so the coefficient governing monomer self-limitation should depend on E through a sharper bounded function rather than a purely linear amplifier.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E, the parent imposes a single smooth monomer-limitation bend through the factor 1 + G/(G_self/(1 + E/E_self_amp)), so increasing E mainly shifts the same G-response earlier without changing its qualitative shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linearized end-amplification of monomer self-limitation with a sharper saturating dependence on E, so the G-response stays near the dilute-end form at low E but bends much earlier and more strongly once E enters an end-rich regime.
response_change.observable_effect: In G sweeps at several fixed E values, low-E curves remain close to the parent dilute-end dependence, while high-E curves show disproportionately stronger early sublinearity than can be matched by a single globally linear E-amplification of G_self.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when comparing G sweeps across dilute to end-rich conditions, especially E around and above E_self_amp with G large enough that monomer-side bending contributes but before any measured regime is dominated solely by the existing joint-load term.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, modest E variation reveals earlier G bending as E rises; in holdout or extended end-rich conditions, the strengthened high-E curvature becomes more pronounced rather than continuing as the parent's single linear trend.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined end-amplification reduces to its linear small-E form over the sampled range, or equivalently when experiments remain in E << E_self_amp so the sharper dependence is not activated.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Local recruitment of monomers into end-dense regions can remain weak over a dilute-to-moderate end range and then saturatingly intensify once many nearby ends compete for the same addable monomer subpool, producing a sharper end-triggered change in apparent monomer availability than a linear amplifier permits.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient multiplying the monomer self-limitation process now changes with E, altering curvature across G sweeps in a condition-dependent way rather than merely rescaling all curves together.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: End-rich demand amplifies monomer self-limitation in a proportionally linear way with E through G_self/(1 + E/E_self_amp).
evolution_contract.assumption_after: End-rich demand amplifies monomer self-limitation through a sharper bounded dependence on E, remaining near-linear at dilute E but saturating in end-rich conditions.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: k_on * G * E / ((1 + G / (G_self / (1 + E / E_self_amp))) * (1 + E / E_crowd + G * E / GE_access))
evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_on * G * E / ((1 + G / (G_self / (1 + E / (E_self_amp + E)))) * (1 + E / E_crowd + G * E / GE_access))
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For E << E_self_amp, E/(E_self_amp + E) ≈ E/E_self_amp, recovering the parent monomer-side modulation over the sampled range.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed low E, v_inc versus G remains close to the parent dilute-end shape; at fixed high E near or above E_self_amp, the monomer-response bends earlier and more sharply before the pre-existing joint-load suppression fully dominates. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the static input-output surface in (G, E) itself acquires stronger high-E curvature.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both conditions because its end effect enters monomer self-limitation only through the globally linear factor 1 + E/E_self_amp. Retuning G_self and E_self_amp can shift the bend location uniformly with E, but cannot keep low-E curves nearly unchanged while simultaneously creating the disproportionately sharper early sublinearity required at end-rich E without spoiling the intermediate-E trend.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when comparing G sweeps across dilute to end-rich conditions, especially E around and above E_self_amp with G large enough that monomer-side bending contributes but before any measured regime is dominated solely by the existing joint-load term.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, modest E variation reveals earlier G bending as E rises; in holdout or extended end-rich conditions, the strengthened high-E curvature becomes more pronounced rather than continuing as the parent's single linear trend.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined end-amplification reduces to its linear small-E form over the sampled range, or equivalently when experiments remain in E << E_self_amp so the sharper dependence is not activated.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model already lets exposed ends amplify monomer self-limitation, but it assumes that amplification grows with a single linear-in-E factor and therefore enforces one-phase curvature change across all end densities.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: End-rich demand amplifies monomer self-limitation in a proportionally linear way with E through G_self/(1 + E/E_self_amp).
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Local recruitment of monomers into end-dense regions can remain weak over a dilute-to-moderate end range and then saturatingly intensify once many nearby ends compete for the same addable monomer subpool, producing a sharper end-triggered change in apparent monomer availability than a linear amplifier permits.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase assumption for how exposed-end abundance modifies monomer self-limitation. The parent already contains this mechanism, so add_term is not appropriate; the issue is the idealized mathematical form. The concrete distinguishing condition is: vary G, hold all parameters fixed, and compare incorporation curves at low versus high fixed E. In the parent, raising E only rescales the same monomer self-crowding denominator through 1 + E/E_self_amp, so one parameter set can shift the G bend earlier but cannot create a noticeably sharper high-E transition while keeping low-E behavior nearly unchanged. A child with a sharper saturating E-dependence changes the target mapping itself: at low E it tracks the parent, but once E approaches or exceeds the amplification scale, the slope of v_inc versus G drops earlier and curvature increases more abruptly. This is scientifically admissible in end-rich intracellular regions where many nearby polymerizing ends draw on a partially shared immediately addable monomer pool. The effect is visible only when both G and E are large enough for monomer-side limitation to matter; if all sampled E are dilute or all G are too low, the refinement will be weak and the parent effectively recovered.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: Permeabilized cells are supplied with independently varied concentrations of polymerization-competent actin monomers and exposed filament ends. The immediate gross incorporation rate into intracellular actin filaments is measured before monomer depletion or filament remodeling becomes appreciable. Each accessible end is treated as an equivalent incorporation site, and addition events depend on encounters with available monomers. The response should increase separately with both monomer abundance and exposed-end abundance.
